主要内容: On March 25, 2015, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) adopted final rules to facilitate smaller companies’ access to capital. These rules, known as Regulation A+, update and expand Regulation A, an existing exemption from registration for smaller issuers of securities. The new rules are mandated by Title IV of the Jumpstart Our Business Startups (JOBS) Act. Under the updated exemption, smaller companies can offer and sell up to $50 million of securities in a 12-month period, subject to eligibility, disclosure, and reporting requirements. The rules introduce two tiers of offerings: Tier 1, for up to $20 million in a 12-month period, and Tier 2, for up to $50 million in a 12-month period. Tier 2 offerings also require additional disclosure and ongoing reporting requirements. The rules will be effective 60 days after publication in the Federal Register. The SEC has adopted new rules to facilitate smaller companies' access to capital. These rules, part of the updated Regulation A, aim to provide exemptions from registration requirements for certain offerings. The rules allow companies to raise up to $50 million in a 12-month period, provided they meet specific conditions, including maintaining a public float of less than $75 million or annual revenues of less than $50 million. The rules also exempt Tier 2 offerings from the mandatory registration requirements of Exchange Act Section 12(g). Additionally, the SEC is exploring ways to collaborate with state regulators to implement these rules effectively. The amendments to Regulation A are part of the JOBS Act, which aimed to update and expand the exemption. The rules become effective 60 days after publication in the Federal Register.
